content.title: About
content.content: Dosa is a thin, crispy crepe made from fermented rice and black‑lentil batter, a staple of South Indian cuisine. The version with filling (3890) includes a savory mixture of vegetables, spices and sometimes cheese, making the dish more filling and nutritious.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The batter ferments for 8–12 hours, giving dosa its characteristic tangy flavor.
Dosa is traditionally served with chutney, sambar and a variety of dips.
In South India dosa is called the “king’s breakfast” and is sold at street stalls as well as home kitchens.
There are over 30 dosa varieties, including masala dosa with a spiced potato filling.
Traditionally dosa is cooked on a large cast‑iron skillet called a “tava”.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: The rice‑lentil batter provides slow‑releasing energy, helping to keep you satisfied longer.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many fried foods, dosa is cooked with minimal oil, making it suitable for lighter diets.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Black lentils add a notable amount of protein, beneficial for muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and gut microbiota.

items.title: B‑vitamin content
items.content: Fermentation boosts B1, B2 and B6 levels, which aid nerve function and metabolism.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to the lentils used in the batter.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Traditional dosa is gluten‑free, but some recipes add wheat flour; check the ingredient list if you have celiac disease.

items.title: Salt in accompaniments
items.content: Chutneys and sambar can be high in sodium; people with hypertension should watch portion sizes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the filled dosa hot, folded or rolled into a cone. It’s eaten by hand, accompanied by chutney, yogurt dip or sambar. Fillings can vary – vegetables, cheese, chicken or seafood.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Freshly made dosa is best eaten within 2–3 hours. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours; reheat briefly on a dry skillet to restore crispness.

egg-substitute-omelet-scrambled-or-fried.title: Egg substitute, omelet, scrambled, or fried with cheese, meat and vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Egg substitute is a ready‑to‑use blend that allows you to make an omelet, scrambled eggs or fried dishes without real eggs. It typically contains plant proteins, starch, vegetable oil, flavorings and sometimes additives that mimic the taste and texture of eggs. The product is suitable for vegetarians, vegans and people with egg allergies.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg substitute is widely used in restaurants for quick preparation of egg‑style dishes without actual eggs.
The mix can be fortified with vitamins B12 and D to compensate for nutrients missing in regular eggs.
Some brands add turmeric or food coloring to imitate the yellow hue of egg yolk.
It has a long shelf life and does not require refrigeration before opening.
Using egg substitute can lower dietary cholesterol because it contains no animal fats.

items.title: Low cholesterol
items.content: Absence of animal fats makes the substitute heart‑friendly.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: The blend includes soy or pea protein isolate, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Added B2, B6 and B12 help energy metabolism.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Starch and dietary fiber in the formula can aid normal bowel function.

items.title: Allergy‑friendly
items.content: No egg protein makes it safe for those with egg allergies.

items.title: Soy/pea protein allergy
items.content: Some substitutes contain soy isolate, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt is often added for flavor; people monitoring sodium should check the label.

items.title: Artificial additives
items.content: Certain versions include flavorings and colorants that may not suit those avoiding synthetic ingredients.

items.title: Missing micronutrients
items.content: Unlike real eggs, the substitute may lack iron and selenium in adequate amounts.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Mix the powder with water (or plant milk) according to package directions, usually 1:1, whisk until smooth and fry in a lightly oiled pan. Add cheese, diced meat and vegetables as desired, cooking it like a regular omelet or scrambled eggs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed container. After opening, keep refrigerated and use within 4–6 weeks.

content.title: About
content.content: Jai is a ready‑to‑eat vegetarian meal kit from Monk's Food, providing 5 balanced servings designed to sustain energy and fullness throughout the day. The product is based on plant proteins, whole grains and vegetables, and contains no GMOs, gluten or artificial additives.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Each serving provides roughly 400 kcal, making it convenient for calorie‑controlled diets.
The formula includes pea and soy proteins, delivering a complete profile of essential amino acids.
Monk's Food uses only certified organic ingredients grown without pesticides.
The product is packaged in biodegradable containers, reducing environmental impact.
Jai was developed in collaboration with nutritionists to achieve an optimal protein‑fat‑carbohydrate ratio.

items.title: High plant‑based protein
items.content: Pea and soy proteins support muscle maintenance and accelerate recovery after exercise.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Whole grains and vegetables provide fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The balanced carbohydrate blend helps maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: The kit contains vitamins B1, B2, B6 and B12, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals and antioxidants
items.content: Includes magnesium, iron and polyphenols that support nervous system function and protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Soy protein is present and may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Moderate sodium content
items.content: Salt is added for flavor; people monitoring sodium intake should account for this.

items.title: Not suitable for children under 3
items.content: Texture and portion size could pose a choking hazard for young children.

items.title: Phytic acid presence
items.content: Pea protein contains phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption if consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the ready‑to‑eat meal in the microwave for 2–3 minutes or on the stovetop, then stir. You can enhance the dish with fresh vegetables, herbs, or nuts for added flavor and texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, keep the product in the refrigerator and consume within 3–5 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Roasted potato is a dish made from fresh tubers that are peeled, cut into pieces and fried until a golden crust forms. The peel is left on and eaten, preserving most of the fiber and micronutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato is the fourth most produced agricultural crop worldwide.
Frying creates a characteristic aroma through Maillard reactions.
The edible peel contains more fiber, vitamin C, and potassium than the flesh.
Traditionally fried potatoes are cooked in vegetable oil, but olive or avocado oil can be used for a healthier version.
Different countries have their own names: in France “frites”, in Spain “patatas bravas”, in Russia “жареный картофель”.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide slowly digestible energy, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C in the peel supports immune function and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium aids normal heart and muscle function.

items.title: Fiber content
items.content: The peel adds dietary fiber, improving digestion and satiety.

items.title: Low in fat when cooked modestly
items.content: With a moderate amount of oil, roasted potatoes remain a low‑fat food.

items.title: High calories with excess oil
items.content: Using too much oil raises the calorie count and may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Acrylamide formation on over‑cooking
items.content: Over‑frying can produce acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound.

items.title: Rare potato allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to potatoes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Roasted potatoes are served as a side dish, in wedges, cubes or sticks. They can be seasoned with salt, spices, herbs, or accompanied by sauces such as ketchup, mayo, or sour cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked roasted potatoes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in the oven or skillet to restore crispness.

content.title: About
content.content: Enfamil Enfagrow is a toddler milk formula designed for children aged 1 to 3 years. It provides a balanced blend of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins, minerals, as well as DHA and ARA to support brain and eye development.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The formula is enriched with prebiotics that promote a healthy gut microbiome.
It contains a complex of B‑vitamins important for energy metabolism.
Enfamil Enfagrow has undergone clinical trials confirming its safety and efficacy.
Available in various package sizes, from 400 g to 900 g.
The product does not contain artificial colors or flavors.

items.title: Supports brain development
items.content: DHA and ARA help form neural connections and support visual function in toddlers.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Vitamins A, C, D and zinc aid the body’s defense mechanisms.

items.title: Promotes bone health
items.content: Calcium, phosphorus and vitamin D contribute to bone growth and mineralization.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Prebiotics and easily digestible proteins reduce the risk of constipation and support comfortable digestion.

items.title: Provides steady energy
items.content: Balanced carbohydrates and fats deliver a stable energy supply throughout the day.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Children allergic to cow’s milk may react; a hypoallergenic formula should be used instead.

items.title: Caloric excess
items.content: Over‑feeding can lead to unwanted weight gain; follow the recommended serving sizes.

items.title: Improper reconstitution
items.content: Too concentrated a mixture can strain the kidneys, while overly diluted formula may not meet nutritional needs.

items.title: Storage after preparation
items.content: Prepared formula should be used within 24 hours to prevent bacterial growth.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Mix the specified amount of powder with warm (not hot) water according to the package instructions. Serve to the child in a bottle or cup. If desired, a small amount of breast milk can be added.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the dry powder in its original sealed container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Use within 30 days after opening. Prepared formula can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours.
